title: Regional SKU transit buckets and commit phasing
summary: Working sheet proposing a complementary framework to classical safety-stock: define in-transit buckets (fast, variable, drawn-out) by region and SKU, then phase financial commitments across tranches to smooth lead-time risk and optimize utilization. Contains example numeric scenarios for AU/US/EU/APAC and recommended immediate actions.
assumptions: Lead times: A100 (45-75 days), H100 (75-120 days), L40 (30-60 days). Minimum order unit (MOU) per vendor: 16 GPUs. Typical monthly burn (tokens->gpu-hours mapping) normalized to GPU-weeks. Customs+logistics variance add +/- 14 days for APAC and +7 days for EU during Q4. We assume 10% weekly variance in demand for latency workloads and 25% for batch training surges.
body:
Context:
- Problem: high variance in arrival windows causes overcommit or brittle shortfalls for latency customers. Current procurement is large single-commit orders which either arrive too late or create large idle pools in some regions.
- Goal: reduce shortfall probability below 5% while keeping average idle < 8% across regions.

Proposed framework (high level):
1) Define three transit buckets per region: FAST (expected lead < 45d), MID (45-90d), SLOW (>90d). Buckets are defined by vendor, transport mode, customs exposure.
2) Map each SKU into buckets using vendor historical lead distributions.
3) Phase financial commitments into tranches: reserve (30% upfront for FAST-capable vendors), staging (40% at MID expected delivery window), backstop (30% for SLOW or optional leasing).
4) Use a rolling 12-week window to re-evaluate bucket assignments and reallocate staging funds.

Example numeric table (snapshot, GPU-weeks = capacity weeks for expected fleet):
Region | SKU | Current Fleet | Committed 0-30d | Committed 31-90d | Pipeline uncertain (>90d) | Monthly burn (gpu-weeks) | Safety target (gpu-weeks) | Suggested tranche this quarter
West-US | A100 | 480 | 32 | 128 | 64 | 220 | 300 | +64 (MID tranche, split 32/32)
East-US | H100 | 240 | 0 | 64 | 96 | 110 | 150 | +32 (reserve FAST vendor pilot + 32 leasing)
West-EU | A100 | 200 | 16 | 48 | 80 | 95 | 140 | +48 (prioritize FAST shipments to EU port; staging 40/60)
APAC | L40 | 160 | 8 | 16 | 48 | 125 | 180 | +0 (increase backstop leasing, defer large purchase until customs window shrinks)
Global | mixed | 1080 | 56 | 256 | 288 | 550 | 770 | Tranche plan: 5 x 16-unit MOUs across vendors split by bucket

Risk bucketing notes:
- FAST bucket vendors: small capacity but predictable air freight windows, ideal for burst/latency-sensitive lanes. Prioritize token-latency customers.
- MID bucket: ocean + consolidated air, moderate variance; good for replenishment to maintain utilization target.
- SLOW: direct factory shipments, high volume discounts but delivery uncertainty; use for opportunistic cost play and base capacity only when safety target exceeded.

Procurement phasing examples and cash flow impact:
- Quarter example (Q4): total planned commits = 160 GPUs. Phase: Reserve 48 (30%) at contract signature (30d cash flow hit), Staging 64 (40%) 30-60d, Backstop 48 (30%) contingent/invoice on arrival. Cash smoothing reduces monthly CapEx by ~28% relative to single lump commit.

Operational considerations and constraints:
- Minimum order units require some region bundling to hit MOUs; recommend cross-region pooling agreement for vendor X to combine 16-unit MOUs across West-US + East-US when customs risk is low.
- Leasing: keep a standing 64-GPU lease pool (rotating) to act as backstop for APAC during Q4. Leasing cost ~2.2x per-week than owned marginal cost but reduces downtime risk for latency SLAs.
- Warranty/returns: expected ~1% RMA within 12 months; schedule a 6-week buffer in MID bucket for refurbishment/rotation.

Open questions:
- Do we want fixed percentage tranche split as default (30/40/30) or region-adaptive splits based on customs variance?
- Vendor-specific reliability data is incomplete for two OEMs in APAC (need historical PO lead logs).
- Should we centralize staging funds under finance or let region owners trigger staging releases?

Immediate action items (owner):
- Alex Cheng: request vendor lead-time CSV exports for last 18 months (due 2024-09-24).
- Priya Nair: prototype tranche cash-flow model in the procurement sandbox (due 2024-09-30).
- Daniel Park: pilot FAST bucket lease agreement with vendor Y for West-US (start 2024-10-01).

Appendix: quick sensitivity check (two scenarios)
- Conservative demand spike (+25%): shortfall probability with no phasing = 38%, with 30/40/30 phasing + 64-GPU lease backstop = 6%
- Customs disruption (APAC +14d avg lead): MID->SLOW reclassification increases Idle by 3% unless staging reallocated from EU to APAC

Notes to reviewers: rough numbers intentionally rounded. This sheet is a living artifact to capture debate before creating a formal procurement playbook. Add comments inline or append notes and tag with JIRA keys.
